entries.intent: Bind a value that depends on a condition and use it afterwards.
entries.applicability: Two-way choice whose result feeds a later expression. Form c (return in each branch) only applies when the value is returned immediately and the continuation is tiny (here `*x+g`, 5 bytes); it duplicates the continuation, so with any reused or longer continuation the expression-if bind (a) wins. Form b is the mut-flag anti-pattern (idiom rule 1).
entries.card_rule: if: return per branch, never mut flag

candidates.label: expression-if bound with let — expected: tied (branch only, no alloc)
mut-flag then if/el assigns — expected: tied
statement-if returning from each branch — expected: tied

entries.intent: Choose one of several values from an ordered set of threshold tests.
entries.applicability: Three or more mutually exclusive conditions tested in order (grades, buckets, tiers). Form c (a ladder of independent ifs overwriting one mut) is only equivalent when later tests subsume earlier ones, so it is fragile as well as verbose.
entries.card_rule: el if chain, never nested if/el

candidates.label: `el if` chain as one expression — expected: tied
mut-flag ladder of independent ifs — expected: tied (evaluates every test)

entries.intent: Compute a value from the OR of two tests.
entries.applicability: Any boolean combination; `&&`/`||` short-circuit. Form b (flag soup) evaluates every test; form c (sequential early returns) works only when the result is returned directly.
entries.card_rule: combine tests in one expr-if, no flags

candidates.label: flag soup: two ifs setting one mut — expected: tied

entries.intent: Clamp a value into [lo,hi] (min/max).
entries.applicability: Any bounded value; the stdlib has no min/max combinators (ABSENT per combinator-status), so an expression-if chain is the primitive. A helper-function form was not measured because helper bodies fall outside the counted `pat` region.
entries.card_rule: clamp: one el if chain expression

candidates.label: mut copy then two clamping ifs — expected: tied
two guard returns then value — expected: tied

entries.intent: Render a boolean test as the text `true`/`false`.
entries.applicability: Printing or storing a bool as text. Interpolating a bool prints `1`/`0` on tkc 2.8.0 (127.15), so form b changes the output and is blocked; 8.5% of corpus programs hand-write a boolstr helper for this (131.30).
entries.card_rule: bool text: expr-if picks the literal

candidates.label: expression-if selecting the literal — expected: tied (no alloc: literal returned)
mut string flag overwritten by an if — expected: tied

bug_caveats.effect: `"\(x%2==0)"` prints 1/0, not true/false — checksum differs (len=1000 vs 4500 at PAT_N=1000)

entries.intent: Sum the elements of an @i64.
entries.applicability: Numeric reduction over an array. The reduce form needs a two-arg helper function (`addf`) declared outside `pat`; its tokens are not counted in the measured region, so the token tie flatters b. `fold` is ABSENT (127.4); `reduce` is the canonical combinator.
entries.card_rule: sum: lp into a mut, not reduce

candidates.label: lp accumulating into a mut — expected: best (inlined add, no calls)
`xs.reduce(0;&addf)` — expected: slower (indirect call per element through tk_arr_reduce; helper not inlined)

bug_caveats.effect: `xs.fold` links against an undefined symbol; `xs.reduce(init;&f)` is the working equivalent and is what form b uses

entries.intent: Count the elements satisfying a predicate.
entries.applicability: Count with a per-element test. Forms b and c need a helper predicate/step function outside `pat` (not counted). b materialises the filtered array just to take its length.

candidates.label: lp with if and counter — expected: best (no alloc, no calls)
`xs.filter(&p).len` — expected: slower (allocates an N-slot result array + indirect call per element)
`xs.reduce(0;&step)` with expr-if step — expected: slower (indirect call per element)

entries.intent: Find the minimum (symmetrically maximum) of a non-empty @i64.
entries.applicability: Non-empty arrays only (all forms index element 0). `min`/`max` combinators are ABSENT. Form c sorts a copy (qsort, O(N log N), one N-word allocation) to read element 0; its 4N/N ratio stays within 1.5x of linear so the protocol classes it `slower`, not `worse-bigO` — hence the hot_path rule.

candidates.label: lp tracking the running minimum — expected: best (O(N), no alloc)
`xs.sort(&cmp).get(0)` — expected: slower (qsort O(N log N) + full copy)

verdict.choose_hot_path_when: arrays larger than ~1k elements, or the minimum is taken inside a loop body: sort is O(N log N) plus a full copy, the loop is O(N) with no allocation

entries.intent: Accumulate values into a new @i64 in a loop.
entries.applicability: Any loop that collects results. `x=x.append(v)` at a self-update site is lowered to the in-place amortised append (ADR-0006 D2); `x=x+@(v)` calls tk_array_concat, which mallocs and copies the whole array every iteration (O(N^2) bytes, never freed). std.vec is a separate handle type needing `vec.toarray` at the end.

candidates.label: `x=x+@(v)` — expected: worse-bigO (concat copies the array each step)
std.vec push then toarray — expected: tied (amortised push, one final copy)

entries.intent: Accumulate per-key totals for a small fixed key set.
entries.applicability: Keys drawn from a known set of ~4 strings. Both forms are a linear key scan (the 2.8.0 map is an unsorted entry list searched with strcmp; `m.set` updates in place). Form b only applies when the key set is fixed and small; with an open key set the map is the only correct form. Int-keyed maps crash on 2.8.0, so keys must be str.

candidates.label: seeded map, `m=m.set(k;m.get(k)+v)` — expected: tied (in-place put, strcmp scan of 4 entries)
parallel arrays + linear key search + `c=c.set(j;…)` — expected: tied (4 string compares, in-place set)

entries.intent: Remove duplicate values from an @i64 (order not significant).
entries.applicability: Dedupe where result order is free (checksum is len+sum). Form a (array `.contains`) is the natural form but segfaults on 2.8.0 (127.11). Form d keys a map by the interpolated value: one interpolation alloc per element and a linear strcmp scan of the seen-set, so it is quadratic like b.
entries.card_rule: dedupe: sort a copy, append if != prev

candidates.label: inner lp scan with flag+br, then append — expected: worse-bigO (O(N·distinct))
sort a copy, append when != previous — expected: best (qsort O(N log N) + in-place appends)
seen-map keyed by `"\(v)"` — expected: worse-bigO (linear-scan map + 1 alloc per element)

bug_caveats.effect: array receiver `.contains` is routed to the str glue and SIGSEGVs with a clean check

entries.intent: Build one string from N parts in a loop.
entries.applicability: Any loop that appends text. `s.concat` allocates a fresh copy of the whole accumulator each step (O(N^2) bytes, never freed); the builder grows one buffer; append+join appends in place and allocates once at join.

candidates.label: `r=s.concat(r;part)` chain — expected: worse-bigO (copies the accumulator per step)
`acc=acc.append(part)` then `s.join("";acc)` — expected: tied (in-place append + one join alloc)

entries.intent: Assemble a 3-5 part string from values of mixed type.
entries.applicability: Templating a fixed number of parts. Interpolation lowers to one tk_str_join_n call (1 alloc); `s.join` needs an array literal plus `s.fromint` for the number (3 allocs); nested `s.concat` allocates per step (5 allocs).

candidates.label: nested `s.concat` chain — expected: slower (alloc per concat)

source: card:interpolation — PREFERRED for all templating and multi-part strings

entries.intent: Convert an i64 to its decimal string.
entries.applicability: Number to text with no width/precision. All three forms reach tk_str_fromi64 (1 alloc). `n as str` is accepted by 2.8.0 although the card lists only numeric casts.

entries.intent: Left-pad a number's text to a fixed width with spaces.
entries.applicability: Fixed-width formatting (tables, ids). Widths are small constants, so every form is a handful of allocations; `s.repeat(str;u64)` exists in 2.8.0 and interpolates correctly. Forms c/d guard `p>0` because `s.repeat` takes a u64.

candidates.label: lp prepending with `s.concat` — expected: tied (≤w small allocs)
builder: add spaces then the digits — expected: tied

entries.intent: Collect N labels into a @str, then render each one.
entries.applicability: The collect-then-format shape of CLI/report tasks. Interpolating an element of a `.append`-built `mut.@()` prints an address on 2.8.0 (127.10: the array is never inferred `@str`), so the natural form a is blocked; form b uses the only append form that tags the array (`+@()`) but copies the array every iteration; form c keeps `.append` and reads elements directly into the builder.

candidates.label: `+@()`-built, interpolated read — expected: worse-bigO (array concat copies per append)
`.append`-built, direct `s.add(b;labels.get(i))` reads — expected: best (in-place append, builder)

source: card:Strings built BY interpolation then stored with arr.append in a loop DANGLE

bug_caveats.effect: `"\(labels.get(i))"` on a `.append`-built array prints pointers (len=12872 vs 5890 at PAT_N=1000); reclassified in 127-disposition-131.md as a missing @str inference, fix in progress

entries.intent: Call a T!Err function and propagate its error to the caller.
entries.applicability: Only inside a function that itself returns T!Err (else E3020). Form b re-wraps the error by hand; `!` is the direct form.
source: card:! propagates — ONLY inside functions that themselves return T!Err

entries.intent: Turn a T!Err result into a plain value with a default on error.
entries.applicability: Consuming an error union where a sentinel is acceptable. Form b avoids the union by re-checking the precondition and calling a non-failing helper (duplicates the check, only possible when the failure condition is known to the caller). Form c is the single-use-let anti-pattern (mined rank 33).

candidates.label: precondition if + plain call — expected: tied

entries.intent: Validate arguments and return sentinels before the main computation.
entries.applicability: Guard clauses at the top of a function. Form b nests each guard in the previous one's else; form c is a single expression-if chain — equal in tokens to a, slightly longer in bytes.

candidates.label: nested if/el with returns — expected: tied
`<if … el if … el{…}` expression — expected: tied

entries.intent: Read typed fields (i64, str) out of a JSON document.
entries.applicability: Any structured JSON input. json.dec + typed accessors is the only form that is correct on reordered keys, whitespace, escapes and nesting; the hand-scan forms are sketches that only work on a fixed layout. Runtime gap: json.dec allocates a heap Json per decode; json.i64 returns the 0 sentinel as $err (a field whose value is 0 is indistinguishable from a missing field); json.arr always returns $err on 2.8.0 (131.30 gap).

verdict.choose_hot_path_when: Fixed, machine-generated layout parsed inside a loop body executed > 100k times AND profiling shows json.dec on the hot path; never for external input (hand scans are incorrect on reordered/escaped JSON). (expected; runtime deferred, loadavg>100)

entries.intent: Split CSV text into rows of fields.
entries.applicability: b (s.split on newline then comma) is only correct for unquoted fields; a (csv.parse) is required whenever fields may be quoted or contain separators/newlines (RFC 4180). csv.parse takes [byte] so the input needs s.bytes(txt); rows are csvrow structs, read fields via rows.get(r).fields. Interpolating a csv field element prints a pointer (127.7 class) - print it directly or use s.len.

bug_caveats.effect: interpolating rows.get(r).fields.get(j) prints a pointer (untagged @str from a module call); checksum uses s.len only

entries.intent: Split one line on a single-character delimiter into a field array.
entries.applicability: Any delimiter split where empty fields must be preserved. s.split is 5-7x fewer tokens than either manual form and is the only one that does not re-scan the string; b re-slices the remainder every iteration (quadratic in fields x line length).

entries.intent: Split a line on whitespace runs, dropping empty fields.
entries.applicability: Whitespace tokenising (A6). s.fields is canonical; b (split on " " + skip empties) is what LLMs write when they forget fields exists. Direct reads of fields elements are correct; interpolating an element prints a pointer until 127.9 lands - use io.println(x) or s.len.

bug_caveats.effect: "\(s.fields(x).get(i))" prints a pointer; fixture checksums use s.len only

entries.intent: Parse a decimal integer string, yielding a default on failure.
entries.applicability: Any int parse. mt s.toint is 9 tokens vs 25 for a digit loop and handles sign/overflow. Note s.toint result 0 is indistinguishable from $err under mt on 2.8.0 (0 sentinel) when the text is "0".
entries.card_rule: parse int: mt s.toint(txt) with default

entries.intent: Turn key=value lines into a str->str map.
entries.applicability: Config-style text. Both forms need a seeded map literal (mut.@() as a map crashes with RT003 on set - 131.30 gap) so the sentinel key "" is present; keys() on a map returned from a user function fails to link (undefined _keys), so the checksum is computed in a helper that receives the map as a typed parameter. String values read back from the map interpolate as pointers (127.7 class); use io.println(v) or s.len(v).
entries.card_rule: k=v lines: s.split twice, then m.set

verdict.choose_hot_path_when: Millions of lines: b allocates two strings per line, a allocates a 2-element array plus two strings per line. (expected; runtime deferred, loadavg>100)

bug_caveats.effect: "\(m.get(k))" on a str-valued map prints a pointer

entries.intent: Transform every element of an array with a per-element function.
entries.applicability: Pure per-element transforms with a named function (&f). Keep a lp when the body is stateful or needs the index.

entries.intent: Keep the elements that satisfy a predicate.
entries.applicability: Predicate is a named bool function. Element interpolation of the result: safe for @i64; for @str the filter result is untagged (127.10 class) - read elements directly.

entries.intent: Sum the elements that satisfy a predicate.
entries.applicability: Filter-then-aggregate. c folds the predicate into a single reduce (one pass, no intermediate array); a allocates the filtered array; b is the inline single loop. Likely hot-path split: b has no indirect call per element.

verdict.choose_hot_path_when: Arrays > 100k elements or a loop body executed > 1k times: the inline loop avoids the per-element indirect call of reduce and the intermediate array of filter. (expected; runtime deferred, loadavg>100)

entries.intent: Return the first element satisfying a predicate, or a default.
entries.applicability: Early-exit search. a returns directly from inside the loop (no flag, no br); b scans everything and allocates; c is the mut-flag scan. xs.find(v) is by value, not predicate, and segfaults on arrays (127.11) so it is not a candidate here (see coll-membership).

entries.intent: Count the elements satisfying a predicate.
entries.applicability: No count/any/all combinator exists on 2.8.0 (ABSENT - 131.30 gap: xs.count(&p) would be ~9 tokens). a allocates the filtered array only to read .len; b is the plain loop; c is a reduce with the predicate folded.

entries.intent: Find the first (i,j) pair in a nested loop and stop.
entries.applicability: Nested search inside a function: return directly with < from the inner loop (a) instead of a found-flag plus two br (b). Only applies when the search is its own function; inline searches in main still need br.
entries.card_rule: nested lp: return directly, no flag

candidates.label: mut flag + br in both loops

entries.intent: Read a map value, substituting a default when the key is missing.
entries.applicability: str-keyed maps. m.get(k) on a missing key returns 0 and mt treats the 0 sentinel as $err, so BOTH forms conflate a stored 0 with "missing"; there is no m.has (m.contains silently returns 0 for present keys) - 131.30 gap. The mt arm cannot appear inside a binary expression (t=t+mt ... is E2002); bind it with let first.

entries.intent: Count how many query values occur in a reference array.
entries.applicability: Repeated membership tests. b (linear scan per query) is O(N*Q) and worse-bigO; a builds a str-keyed map once (int-keyed map literals @(0:1) segfault on .set - 131.30 gap - so keys are "\(x)"). The preferred xs.contains(v) form is blocked by 127.11 (routed to the string glue, SIGSEGV) and would still be O(N*Q).

candidates.label: linear scan with br per query

bug_caveats.effect: array .contains/.find/.indexof/.slice dispatch to the str glue and segfault; c.blocked.tk is the natural form

entries.intent: Sort ascending and take the first k elements.
entries.applicability: Top-k. a sorts (comparator &cmp returns a-b) then copies k elements; b does k selection passes (O(N*k), linear for fixed k but 2x the tokens). The natural xs.sort(&cmp).slice(0;k) is blocked by 127.11.

bug_caveats.effect: array .slice segfaults; c.blocked.tk (sort().slice(0;k)) is the preferred form

entries.intent: Group values by a derived string key into a map of arrays.
entries.applicability: Grouping. a: map of arrays with mt-get-or-empty then set; b: parallel keys/groups arrays with a linear key scan (O(N*K)). Map literal must be seeded (mut.@("":@())) because an empty map literal crashes on set (131.30 gap); the checksum is computed inside pat because .keys() on a map returned from a user function fails to link.
entries.card_rule: group-by: map of arrays, mt get + set

candidates.label: map of arrays via mt get-or-@() + set

entries.intent: Produce the reversed copy of an array.
entries.applicability: No reverse combinator exists (131.30 gap). a appends from the end; b copies and swaps in place; c prepends with @(x)+r and is quadratic (each + copies the accumulator) - token-tied with a but worse-bigO, so it must never be taught.
entries.card_rule: reverse: lp from the end, append

candidates.label: copy + set swap to the middle

entries.intent: Swap two elements of an array.
entries.applicability: Any element swap (sort inner loops). Chained r=r.set(i;r.get(j)).set(j;r.get(i)) is correct under value semantics (the second r.get reads the original) and one token cheaper than the tmp form the card shows; verified byte-identical output.

candidates.label: let tmp + two set statements (card form)

entries.intent: Count (or collect) the distinct values of an array.
entries.applicability: Dedupe. b (nested scan over the unique list) is token-best but O(N*U) - worse-bigO when uniques grow with N - so the map-as-set form is canonical without a hot path. Int-keyed maps segfault (131.30 gap), so the set key is "\(x)".

entries.intent: Read the first program argument with a default when absent.
entries.applicability: args.get(n) returns $err past the end, so mt is a one-expression form; the count check is 7 tokens more. The args.get result interpolates as a pointer (127.7 class) - print it directly or take s.len. args.count() includes the program name.

entries.intent: Drop --flag arguments from an argv array.
entries.applicability: The D-CLI "nonflags" shape: filter with a named predicate vs loop+if+append. The loop form builds with r=r+@(x) because an .append-built @str interpolates as pointers until 127.10 lands; the filter result is read directly in the fixture.

bug_caveats.effect: .append-built string arrays print addresses when an element is interpolated; the loop form uses +@() instead

entries.intent: Format a labelled result as "key=value".
entries.applicability: The 8.5% io.println(show(x)) shape (131.3). For i64/str values interpolation is the best form today; there is no show for bool (prints 1/0 - 127.15) or for arrays/maps (131.30 stdlib gap - a stdlib show/fmt would replace the hand formatters). Values derived from method calls interpolate as pointers (127.7).

bug_caveats.effect: bools interpolate as 1/0, so a bool result still needs a hand formatter
method-call-derived str values print a pointer under interpolation

entries.intent: Test a compound condition inside a loop: named helper or inline expression.
entries.applicability: Protocol region counts only pat: the helper call (16) beats the inline condition (21) but the helper itself costs 14 proxy8k tokens (isok: min_bytes 35), so whole-program the inline form wins for a single call site; a helper pays for itself from the second call site. -O2 is expected to inline the call.
entries.card_rule: compound test: call a named helper

entries.intent: Read one field of a split line.
entries.applicability: Single-use intermediates. Chained postfix (a) and the two-let form (b) count the same proxy8k tokens (11) - the hostile proxy has cheap merges for let - but a is 34 bytes shorter (min_bytes tie-break) and 3 tokens shorter under v03.
entries.card_rule: chain postfix calls, skip interim let

entries.intent: Sum the decimal digits of an integer.
entries.applicability: Depth-bounded recursion (<= 19 frames). Recursion is 5 tokens cheaper; the loop avoids call overhead. Never recurse on unbounded depth (no TCO; stack).

verdict.choose_hot_path_when: The call sits in a loop executed > 1M times, or the recursion depth is data-dependent (stack safety). (expected; runtime deferred, loadavg>100)

entries.intent: Read a file and split it into lines.
entries.applicability: Whole-file reads. No file.readlines exists (131.30 gap); s.split(txt;"\n") yields a trailing "" when the file ends in a newline - both forms keep it. file.read needs --allow-read (fixtures build with --allow-all).

candidates.label: mt file.read + charcode scan + slice per line

entries.intent: Write N lines to a file.
entries.applicability: Append-per-line is token-best (23 vs 27) but reopens the file on every call (a syscall per line, same asymptotic class); the protocol therefore makes it canonical with a hot path - flagged for owner review: a 10-100x constant-factor loss with identical bigO is exactly the case rule 6.4 does not catch. Fixture deletes the file first because file.append accumulates across runs.

verdict.choose_hot_path_when: More than a handful of lines, or any loop: file.append opens/closes the file per call. (expected; runtime deferred, loadavg>100)
